For what follows: You shall not rob, unless referred to this, that harm not be done by robbing, it happens that by not robbing one harms, for a sword is to be taken from a madman. Nor oppress by violence, etc. He gradually instructs the hearer, and joins what seem small to great: that those terrified by the defined punishment of evils may abstain from lesser ones. For those who are partners in the commandment are so in the penalty. For he who offends in one is guilty of all, James 2. Therefore he joins violence to calumny. Nor does it matter how one loses his goods, by fraud or power or any other way. The wages shall not abide, etc. The wages, namely, by which perhaps he lives with wife and children and parents. If it is delayed, food fails; even if he receives it tomorrow, he has borne violence and calumny, because meanwhile he had nothing to live on. The work of the hireling, etc. The wages of the preacher is from the word of preaching: which ought not to abide with us, that is lie idle, till morning, in the future age namely, which succeeds this night, in which is unquenchable light. For from the increase of the disciple grows the reward of the master.
19.14: 19.14 You shall not curse the deaf. To curse the deaf is to detract from one absent and not hearing. To put a stumbling block before the blind is to do a discreet thing, but to give occasion of scandal to one who has not the light of discretion.
19.15: 19.15 You shall not do, etc. ISICHIUS. The highest and perfect justice, etc., down to and to mock the deaf and blind are of the rich and powerful.
19.16: 19.16 You shall not be a detractor. ISICHIUS. Septuagint: You shall not walk in the house, etc., down to who is joined to so great a crime. You shall not stand against. As if you shall not join yourself to those who lie in wait for their neighbors, as many, allied with others, do what they cannot do by themselves.
19.18: 19.18 Seek not revenge. That is, be not carried away by lust of vengeance while you reprove, so that you wish to rejoice or be consoled by another's evil, but rather to advise him whom you reprove. Hence according to the Septuagint follows: You shall not be angry with the sons of your people, etc. For so anger is rightly defined, that it is the lust of revenge.
19.19: 19.19 Your beasts, etc. These according to the letter seem ridiculous, and were not observed by the prophets and spiritual men. Hence David says: Set my son Solomon on my mule, Ecclesiasticus 19. According to the letter, it would be necessary to abominate what was born of such mixture. Hence: The valiant woman shall find wool and flax, and has wrought with the labor of her hands, Proverbs 31.
19.20: 19.20 If a man sleep, etc. ISICHIUS. When he forbade beasts to be mixed with beasts of another kind, those, namely, who are under the yoke of Christ to take the yoke of the law: opportunely he added this, showing that even before the coming of Christ whoever was outwardly mingled with the Jews needed the sacrifice of the true ram. Note how great the difference of freedom and servitude. For in the free betrothed woman death is the penalty of adultery, but in the marriageable handmaid, and, according to the Septuagint, kept for a man, that is betrothed, a sacrifice is commanded to be offered, not death inflicted. Spiritually, however, these are to be understood. Marriageable. Septuagint: Kept for a man, that is the Synagogue kept for the law, who could not be betrothed to Christ before the letter of the law died. Hence: You are dead to the law by the body of Christ, that you may be another's, Romans 7. The handmaid is the Synagogue, according to that: Abraham had two sons, one by a bondwoman, and one by a free woman, Galatians 4. Both shall be scourged. Septuagint: There shall be a visitation for them, that is they shall be freed from the servitude of the law, as is said to the children of Israel to be freed from Egypt: Visiting I have visited you. And they shall not die. For though they acted according to the letter, not the spirit, because they were ignorant of the lawgiver's intention, yet they more easily obtained pardon.
19.23: 19.23 When you are come in, etc. He continues in his purpose, showing that the Jews had not good fruit before the coming of Christ, when he says the fruit is not to be eaten for three years, nor clean, but in the fourth year to be cleansed, nor is it said what the cleansing is. Spiritually therefore what is said is to be understood. When you shall have entered the land. By land he means divine Scripture, which the Jews first received. Hence they were commanded to plant fruit trees. The planting of trees is meditation and preaching of the law, according to that: I planted, Apollos watered, etc., 1 Corinthians 3. The commandments were indeed good like fruit trees, but they did not do what they ought, following the letter only. The fruit therefore, that is the operation of the law, was unclean for three years, from Abraham to David, from David to the transmigration of Babylon; thence to Christ, as Matthew distinguished, Matthew 1. In the fourth year he commends the fruit of the law holy and praiseworthy, yet not yet edible for the Jews. For the fruit of the law in the fourth year, that is at the coming of Christ, holy and praiseworthy, which he made the Holy of holies, whose works are praiseworthy and glorious. Hence in the paralytic carrying his bed they glorified God, Matthew 8., who gave such power to men: but the Jew did not yet eat, because not converted. In the fifth year, however, that is the apostles preaching, whoever believed ate its fruit. And you shall plant, etc. GREGORY, book VIII of Morals, ch. 35. Fruit trees, etc., down to to rejoice in the night of the present life.
19.26: 19.26 You shall not eat, etc. He shaves off the whole leaven of Jews and Gentiles. Hence now he forbids from the servitude of the law, now from the error of the Gentiles. AUGUSTINE. Not to eat on the mountains is not to be fed on proud thoughts, of which Isaiah: Every mountain and hill shall be brought low, Isaiah 40. Not to divine by birds, not to heed what snatch away the seed of piety. To cut the hair round is to consecrate thoughts to demons. To shave the beard is to corrupt the perfection of virtue by feigned working. Not to cut the flesh is not to take up delights, which both harm the soul and corrupt the body. The marks, wicked doctrine, which is fixed in the soul and is hardly effaced. You shall not divine, etc. By a part he signifies the whole, condemning all such superstitions. For he who cares to observe such things seems to defame God, as if he had conferred more knowledge on birds than on men.
19.27: 19.27 Neither shall you cut your hair round, etc. As the barbarians do: each ought to be content with natural ornaments, lest he seem to accuse the Creator as unable to perfect his work, nor in honor of demons nourish and cherish curls, as the pagans are zealous to offer the heads of boys to demons, which he seems chiefly to forbid here.
19.28: 19.28 Marks. The lawgiver also takes care of our comeliness, lest we abuse the flesh even in things which disfigure the body.
19.29: 19.29 Make not your daughter a prostitute. The carnal one, or the soul. Hence Psalm 21: Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog. She, departing from God, fornicates with demons.
19.30: 19.30 Keep my sabbaths. From one sabbath every lawful rest is called sabbath. So from one general abstinence the lawgiver strives to run through singulars, commanding us to abstain from all evil. Hence he adds: And reverence my sanctuary. For as those who approach worthily sanctify, so those who presume wickedly and approach unclean, as much as in them is, pollute, like Nadab and Abihu. Hence the Apostle: Among you many are weak and infirm, etc., 1 Corinthians 11. Thence is added: I am the Lord, holy, namely, and dwelling even in the saints and avenging the injury of the saints.
19.31: 19.31 Go not aside to magicians. Septuagint: Ventriloquists, that is pythons, or false prophets, who from the belly of their heart bring forth certain tales and stinking doctrines. Nor ask of soothsayers, etc. Septuagint: Of sorcerers, who, namely, invoke the names of demons, and sometimes cure the body to kill the soul.
19.32: 19.32 Before the hoary head, etc. In the aged is wisdom, and in length of days prudence, Job 12. Hence Paul says: Let the priests that rule well be esteemed worthy of double honor, especially they who labor in the word and doctrine, 1 Timothy 5.
19.33: 19.33 If a stranger dwell, etc. The land given us by God is the cultivation of virtues, namely, and good doctrine. If anyone therefore wishes to be converted to our faith and be enrolled a citizen of our land, let us not afflict him nor impose a heavy yoke, like the Pharisees, of whom it is said: They bind heavy and insupportable burdens, but with a finger of their own they will not move them, Matthew 23. Let him be to us as a native, who, namely, has been nourished in the faith and grown in piety. Hence Peter to those who wished to circumcise the believers from the Gentiles, says: Why tempt you God, to put a yoke upon the necks of the disciples? Acts 15.
19.35: 19.35 Do not, etc. In the preceding he commands justice to be kept in judgment, here in weights and measures, and that we not abuse the bounds of justice to injustice: for these are bounds for sellers and buyers, as laws for judges; that every injustice against a neighbor be avoided. For what to the rich man is the possessions of fields and treasures of money, this is to the poor the measure of wine and wheat and the like. ISICHIUS. Do not, etc. In the judgment of the mind we ought not to act unjustly, nor corrupt the measures of natural justice, judging otherwise our own sins, otherwise our neighbor's. For with what judgment we judge, we shall be judged; and with what measure we mete, it shall be measured to us again, Matthew 7.
19.36: 19.36 Just balances, etc. THE SAME. Let us also have divine balances and just divine measures; that is, let us keep the laws of divine Scripture holily and justly: bringing in nothing of ours, taking away nothing of his, lest this be said to us: Why do you transgress the commandment of God for your traditions? Matthew 15.
20.1: 20.1 The Lord spoke, etc. The law frequently repeats the same, to fix their memory in the reader: yet it interposes some new things, lest it seem superfluous. But by inquiring into the new, let those already said be more studiously inquired into. Hence above in forbidding some things he was silent on the penalty, that we, seeking what or of what sort it is, may diligently investigate it in what follows. For when above he forbade sacrificing to Moloch, he repeats the same adding the penalty: the people of the land shall stone him, not only the princes. Nor content with this he adds: I will set my face against him, etc.
20.4: 20.4 But if neglecting, etc. He provokes others against him, and terrifies, if they neglect a penalty so studiously commanded, God himself being angry and giving sentence. Nor would he, etc. ISICHIUS. It is evil to permit even those who are without to fornicate from God and cleave to the devil: but much more from the midst of the people, for this is to yield the whole flock to the wolf. The consenting, however, who can accuse, or reprove, or warn, and do not, will not escape judgment. God sets his face upon him, of whom it is said: But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things, etc., Psalm 38.
20.6: 20.6 The soul that shall go aside to magicians, etc. It is a great sin to go aside to magicians and soothsayers: for this is to depart from God. The magicians are intelligible, who prophesy falsehoods in the name of the Lord; the soothsayers are deceivers and flatterers, who with poisonous words corrupt the hearing of many and turn them from the truth.
20.9: 20.9 He that curses his father, etc. ORIGEN, hom. 11 on Leviticus. Of these he gave precepts above, etc., down to lest he punish a contemptuous servant. THE SAME. The name of father or mother, etc., down to do they pervert with depraved senses to some earthly city? His blood, etc. Because he is to himself the cause of death. If he is so punished who curses his carnal father, how shall he be punished who blasphemes Christ, nor obeyed him saying: Unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Spirit, etc., John 3., he shall die the death, namely, alienated from the kingdom of heaven he is guilty: for nothing grievous, nor burdensome, nor laborious is commanded him.
20.10: 20.10 If any man commit adultery, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 73 on Leviticus. Here he wished something to differ, etc., down to than man to man. If he commit adultery, etc. ISICHIUS. Adultery is a corporeal evil, etc., down to who committed this care to him.
20.11: 20.11 He that shall lie, etc. These were said and expounded above, where it was said: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, etc. But here he plainly touches him who does the same as his neighbor, nor blushing at partnership of sin, betrays; in which the lawgiver ordained the penalty of death. He joined the husband of a stepmother, because what a son offends against a father is committed against a son by a father, and the impiety is like on both sides. ORIGEN as above. It was said above, etc., down to not only for the quality but also for the quantity.
20.13: 20.13 He that lies with a male, etc. This sin is an injury to nature: hence it was decreed to be punished with death. Spiritually, let us beware to enfeeble by wicked words or actions him who is strong in mind and male, for a man in divine Scripture is called perfect in virtues, lest we be dissolved with him and die together.
20.14: 20.14 He that shall take, etc. For this offense he decrees a savage penalty. For those born of the mother, with those whom the daughter bore, since the father is one, it is uncertain whether they are brothers or uncles. Let such uncertain mixture be avoided. But because concupiscence is the mother of every sin, if we have any concupiscence, let us not join action to it. For he who does this is burnt with fire, both concupiscence and its action. For if by the spirit we mortify the deeds of the flesh, we shall live, Romans 8.
20.15: 20.15 He that shall lie with a beast, etc. Excessive severity is exercised against those who were so wicked and given to lust as to desire unheard-of crimes: hence to men or women mixed with quadrupeds he decreed the penalty of death. This law will not be superfluous for the faithful either, if we understand quadrupeds as wicked wills prone to the earth: which have not hands like men, because they lack all human action, hence they have no kinship with us. The man or woman therefore who not from weakness of nature but by deliberation cleaves or unites with them is guilty of death. They too are said to die with those killed, for they do not subsist by themselves, nor is there any substance of sin, but it works in sinners. AUGUSTINE. He that shall lie with a beast, etc. It is asked how the beast is guilty, since it is neither rational nor capable of law? or as metaphorical words are transferred from animal to animal; as a wicked wind is said, or an angry sea, so here also transferred from the rational to the irrational? For hence the cattle were commanded to be killed, because, contaminated by such a crime, they revive the unworthy memory of the deed.
20.17: 20.17 He that shall take his sister, etc. ISICHIUS. This seemed tolerable, because Abraham says of Sarah: She is my sister by the father, not by the mother: but Moses, enumerating those born of Terah father of Abraham, never made mention of Sarah. And if Abraham married his sister, he did it before he knew God. Well therefore the law forbade such a union. He that shall take, etc. Tropologically he sees and takes the nakedness of a sister by the father and not by the mother who admires and imitates a base action of the father or mother in which they transgressed: not only searching out what he ought not, but joining himself to the depravity of the parents who is called his sister, as if born of the same parents. Because the sons publish their parents' sins by doing like things, rightly the penalty is inflicted in the sight of the people; or according to the Septuagint: In the sight of the children of their race, of those, namely, who think to imitate such things: that the affliction of one be the correction of many. Shall see the nakedness, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 75. That is, by lying shall know, as there: Adam knew his wife, Genesis 4., that is, was joined to her. And what he says: They shall bear their iniquity, that is, the sin itself was the punishment.
20.20: 20.20 He that shall lie, etc. The lawgiver aims to persuade continence, that we be not continually mixed with women after the manner of cattle, but as if constrained come gradually to the use of continence. It is wonderful, however, that now he commands such to be destroyed from his people, when above he decreed to the same a law of purgation. Let us contemplate then the menstruous wisdom of the Gentiles remote from God, disputing of the flight of birds and the course of stars and the measures of heaven. To sleep with this, that is to take delight, or to reveal and publicly bring forth its turpitude, and to hear it expounding the fountain of all error, is impious. Therefore such a one shall be put to death from the midst of his people, lest he be called a man who by ignorance of the image of God and of himself has alienated the Creator from himself. She too shall be put to death, lest she be called wisdom, because the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God, 1 Corinthians 3. The nakedness, etc. He forbids the sons to be mixed with the sisters of parents, that generations be not confounded and reverence be shown to parents. According to the spirit also we ought to veil the sins of parents, and of those who are allied to them, as brothers and sisters, by whose being laid bare the parents cannot be hid. Hence he adds: He shall uncover the shame of his flesh. Septuagint: They shall die without children, that is without virtues, which is the worst barrenness. He that shall lie, etc. ISICHIUS. He shows that for the sake of children, etc., down to is like the above. AUGUSTINE, question 76 on Leviticus. He that lies with his father's wife, etc. Whoever shall sleep with his kinswoman, etc., down to that is by no right succeed to their parents.
20.22: 20.22 Keep my laws, etc. It is not enough to keep part of the law, we must observe all the precepts and judgments.
20.23: 20.23 Walk not, etc. Not the Jews only but all the nations must observe this if they wish to serve God.
20.24: 20.24 Milk. The delights of beatitude, than which nothing sweeter, nothing more pleasant, and will be without all labor and sorrow, like honey and milk, which are prepared without our labor.
20.26: 20.26 I am the Lord. Think not saying: What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or wherewith shall we be clothed? for after all these things do the heathens seek, Matthew 6. But those who follow a higher conversation and reward ought to be separated from the other nations. Separate, etc. The law calls the beasts or cattle the popular: the birds, the contemplatives. Every popular man is judged clean by many for his simplicity. Likewise the contemplative, but it is not so: the popular ought to be prudent in good, simple in evil, for this alone is clean. The contemplative also ought to have a clean conscience and unfeigned faith. Those who have not these turn aside to vain babbling, understanding neither what they say nor whereof they affirm, 1 Timothy 1. Diligently therefore the clean are to be separated from the unclean, that we may follow the clean and flee the unclean. It is to be noted how discreetly the lawgiver here distinguishes among quadrupeds and birds, and not among creeping things of the earth. For all that move on the earth are unclean, savoring earthly things, whose god is their belly, Philippians 3. And which, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 76 on Leviticus. He seems to say that these are not unclean by nature but for some sign of a sacrament, because he says he showed them unclean, as if they would not be unclean to them unless shown. Stones. Because with vain errors they seduce the simple people; whence they feed the belly and desire to please hearers: of whom there are many today in the Church, of whom Paul says: For they that are such serve not Christ our Lord, but their own belly, and by pleasing speeches and good words seduce the hearts of the innocent, Romans 16.
21.1: 21.1 And the Lord said to Moses: Let not be defiled, etc. ISICHIUS. That is, let him omit nothing of what is expedient to teach the priest, etc., down to for he will not be able to be ignorant of the sin of those who dwell with him.
21.2: 21.2 But only for his near kin. JEROME, letter to Fabiola, vol. 1. Over every soul that is dead, etc., down to but to the lesser something is indulged.
21.5: 21.5 They shall not shave the head. THE SAME, ibid. The high priest, however, etc., down to to whom Christ gave to be light. They shall not shave the head, etc. ISICHIUS. The law forbids priests to grieve too bitterly for the dead, etc., down to that he may be able to exhort, reprove, rebuke. They shall not profane the name, etc. THE SAME. Which is great among the Gentiles. But you, says Malachi, have profaned it in that you say: The table of the Lord is contemptible, Malachi 1. For in the sin of the sacrifice the priests profane the name of God.
21.7: 21.7 A harlot, etc. Any priest, for of the high priest he will say afterward that he take only a virgin to wife. One divorced, etc. Because she is found guilty, the priest ought not to marry her, nor preach her literal observance.
21.8: 21.8 Let them therefore be holy, etc. If the priests keep the sanctification already given them by God, they sanctify God himself: who, though holy in nature, willed to be sanctified by the partakers of his glory.
21.9: 21.9 The priest's daughter, etc. It is grave for anyone's daughter to fornicate, but most of a priest, who ought to have children subject in all chastity. The priest's daughter. The Synagogue is called not only wife but also daughter of God; but depraving both, she became a stranger. Hence: The daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard, etc., Isaiah 1. And elsewhere: Their mother has fornicated, Hosea 2.: that she is burnt with fire the traces of the burning show.
21.10: 21.10 The high priest, etc. Christ, our great Lord, and great is his power, who for us was made priest and victim. Consecrated. Other priests were consecrated or consummated, namely, their hands in the blood of the calf and ram: he with his own blood, with crucified hands. He shall not rend his garments, etc. ISICHIUS. For since the Word was made flesh, etc., down to these are truly holy garments.
21.11: 21.11 To any dead, etc. ISICHIUS. Septuagint: A dead soul. The soul that sins shall die, Ezekiel 18; Isaiah 53. By this death the Gentiles chiefly perished, who had neither law nor doctrine; but Christ bore the sins of all, and yet remained undefiled. AUGUSTINE, question 81 on Leviticus. To any dead, etc. Septuagint: Over any dead soul he shall not enter. How he says a dead soul, etc., down to what the second he did not forbid.
21.12: 21.12 THE SAME, question 82. He shall not go out of the holy places. While, namely, their funerals are celebrated, he is forbidden to go out of the holy places, etc., down to that on some days incense was not laid on. Over his father. ORIGEN, hom. 14 on Leviticus. Every man is defiled in father and mother, etc., down to or defile the liberty of the heavenly mother by unworthy servitude of sin. AUGUSTINE, question 85 on Leviticus. It may be asked, etc., down to as Scripture testifies of Aaron himself. I am the Lord. AUGUSTINE, question 84. Of Moses also it was said, etc., down to nor was the visible sanctification judged superfluous, because the invisible went before.
21.13: 21.13 He shall take a virgin to wife. JEROME, letter to Fabiola. A widow is she whose husband, etc., down to hence: For I have espoused you to one husband, a chaste virgin, etc. I would not that the disciple and spouse of the high priest have anything of the old man. If we have risen with Christ, let us mind the things that are above, forgetful of the past, eager for the future. Unhappy Simon, who after baptism thought of his old marriage and had not come to virginal purity, was unworthy of Peter's fellowship.
21.14: 21.14 But a widow or divorced woman, etc. ORIGEN, hom. 12 on Leviticus. He who sins is cast away; even if the bishop is silent, either from ignorance or negligence, such grace avails not; Christ does not take to wife a cast-away soul, nor a polluted one, that wished and desired so great a sin, for the great high priest requires altogether a pure soul, which he may join to himself and make one spirit. He who sins unto death is cast away; he who venially is polluted. A filthy one, etc. Who goes after lovers, the demons namely, who desire to commit adultery with the beautiful soul, that is, made to the image of God.
21.17: 21.17 A man of the seed. ISICHIUS. These are to be taken only according to the letter, etc., down to greatly by contumely he resists.
21.18: 21.18 If blind. ISICHIUS. Ignorant of the light of contemplation, pressed by the darkness of the present life, who while he does not diligently behold the coming light, knows not whither to stretch the step of work. If lame. THE SAME. Who, namely, sees whither he ought to go, but by weakness of mind cannot do what he desires. If with a small, or great, or crooked nose. THE SAME. He has a small nose who is not fit to hold the measure of discretion: for by the nose we discern odors and stenches. A great and crooked nose is immoderate subtlety of discretion, which growing beyond what is needful or fitting confounds the rectitude of action.
21.19: 21.19 If with a broken foot. ISICHIUS. Who cannot go the way of God and is bereft of good work, not as the lame, who at least held with weakness.
21.20: 21.20 If crookbacked. THE SAME. Pressed by earthly solicitude, not looking to heavenly things, looking only to lower ones. If blear-eyed. The blear-eyed, whose wit shines to the knowledge of truth, but carnal operation darkens. For in the blear-eyed the pupils are sound, but with the humor flowing the eyelids thicken, by whose frequent infusion the sharpness even of the pupil is spoiled. If a film. THE SAME. He has a film who is not suffered to see the light of truth, because he is blinded by arrogance of wisdom or justice. For the black pupil sees, the white does not see: because the sense of human thought if it understands itself foolish or a sinner apprehends the knowledge of inmost clarity: if it ascribes to itself the whiteness of justice or wisdom, it excludes itself from heavenly knowledge. If a continual scab. THE SAME. Over whom, namely, the petulance of the flesh without ceasing rules in the mind. In a scab the heat of the bowels is drawn to the skin, in which luxury is signified, because likewise temptation of the heart leaps forth into action. If a rash in the body. GREGORY, Pastoral, part 1, ch. 11. He has a rash in the body, etc., down to because through all vices it supplants the mind. For the root of all evils is covetousness, 1 Timothy 6. Or ruptured. Others, heavy, because, namely, he does not exercise the foulness in work, but is still burdened in mind by continual thought: who with all his thoughts flows to wantonness, as bearing in the heart the weight of turpitude.
21.21: 21.21 Everyone that has a blemish. Whoever is subject to any of these vices is forbidden to offer bread to the Lord, lest he who is still wasted by his own offenses be unable to wash away those of others. AUGUSTINE, question 35 on Leviticus. All doubt is taken away, etc., down to by whom it was necessary that incense be laid on. The priest ought to be unblemished in mind and conduct, whom as Moses commanded to be clean from twelve blemishes according to the Septuagint: so Paul warned him to keep twelve, saying: Not proud, not angry, not given to wine, etc., 1 Timothy 2. For he is the steward of God, who ought to excel his subjects in virtues. This also is done in the Church if anyone has been blemished and by penance has ceased, he is not forbidden to communicate with the saints: but to minister, or approach the veil and the altar is not lawful. For the veil and the altar is the body of Christ, hence Paul: We have an altar of which they have no power to eat who serve the tabernacle, Hebrews 13. And elsewhere: Having confidence in the entering into the holies by the blood of Christ, a new and living way which he has dedicated for us through the veil, that is his flesh, Hebrews 10. And he ought not to profane, etc. By acting disorderly they would scandalize the people, thinking the ministry of God, and justice and judgment, superfluous.
21.24: 21.24 Moses spoke, etc. He commends the dignity of Moses: to others God speaks few things, to him all things, because he is just and the image of Christ. He warns us also to attend to the greater and more perfect, who continually enjoy the eternal vision.
22.2: 22.2 Which they themselves offer, etc. What they have offered, namely, to the priests, to be offered by them to the Lord. Note the kind of sanctification which is made by the vow and devotion of the offerer; but whether men are said to sanctify themselves in the same way when they vow themselves in some matter is to be observed.
22.3: 22.3 Every man that shall approach, etc. As if, let him not only abstain from the ministry and mystic office, but not touch what has been offered, for the clean ought to approach clean things.
22.4: 22.4 He that is a leper, etc. He does not abominate the sensible leper, who suffers unwillingly, but the spiritual: which he expounds there: He that touches an unclean thing on a dead body, or, according to the Septuagint: Every uncleanness of the soul, that is sin. From which, etc. JEROME, letter to Fabiola. If any of the priests' seed flow, etc., down to let him be held by no other custom.
22.9: 22.9 Let them keep, etc. To those who keep the commandments of the Lord they are the cause of justification and salvation; to transgressors, of sin and death, and chiefly in the reception of holy things. For he that eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, etc., 1 Corinthians 11.
22.10: 22.10 The sojourner of the priest, etc. ISICHIUS. He who lives in the Church not purely nor diligently, as one about to move on, for glory or gain, is remembered as a hireling: who is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, John 10.
22.12: 22.12 Married to any of the people. THE SAME. It is not enough to be nourished in the faith of Christ: we ought to remain and grow in it; nor to be mixed with any foreigners, that is doctrine alien to God, or law or action: nor because we are of faithful fathers let us presume on the holy, but where we ourselves persist faithful.
22.14: 22.14 He that shall eat of the sanctified things, etc. ISICHIUS. The holies of holies, etc., down to Hence Solomon: When you sit to eat with a prince, consider diligently what is set before you, Proverbs 23. He shall add a fifth, etc. Septuagint: Upon it. The fifth therefore not from elsewhere, but from it and with it, or upon it, is commanded to be added: this is the word uttered by Christ himself over the Lord's mystery. He himself removes us from ignorance, nor let anyone think carnal or earthly. This is well called a fifth, because the spirit and the word which he delivers composes our five senses; nor does it bring only taste to the mystery, but hearing and sight and touch and smell, that we suspect nothing earthly of those things that are heavenly. And he shall give to the priest into the sanctuary. ISICHIUS. The sanctification of the mystic sacrifice, and the passage from sensible to intelligible things, must truly be given to the priest: because by his power and word the things that are seen are sanctified, that they may exceed all the senses.
22.15: 22.15 Of the children of Israel. It signifies the faithful people, who through this mystery see God: and whoever consecrate to God for the Lord's sacrifice, they are holy of holies, because from them the body of Christ is made. For he is the first-fruits of our mass: therefore rightly it subsists from our first-fruits.
22.17: 22.17 The Lord spoke, etc. ISICHIUS. Not only the priests, etc., down to for otherwise it will not be accepted.
22.18: 22.18 A man of the house of Israel, etc. According to the letter also, if you offer an ox or sheep or goat, or anything of the kind, giving first-fruits to the priests, or feeding the poor, or constructing divine buildings, or doing anything that pertains to God himself, for therefore it is called holocaust, let this offering be unpolluted; yet he does not name pollution, that we may understand the spiritual pollution which is from robbery, injustice, covetousness, and the like.
22.21: 22.21 The man that shall offer, etc. He commanded the offering of the people to be clean: he adds what sort the ministers ought to be and offer. Of peace offerings, etc. Which avail to salvation and peace: even if he cannot philosophize perfectly, as he who has left all, who studies virginity and the like. For star differs from star in glory, 1 Corinthians 15.
22.22: 22.22 If it be blind, etc. He who knows not God and his ministry cannot expound it to others; hence about himself and about others and about the ministry he acts negligently. Hence: Behold they are all ignorant, dumb dogs not able to bark, Isaiah 56. If broken. In foot or hand: whose action, namely, or will is weak or distorted, is not worthy of salvation and the holy altars. If a scar. He marks the detractor: for he is worst in morals and a very harsh wound is not easily mitigated. If pustules. Septuagint: a cut tongue: who, namely, on account of a filthy life has lost confidence in teaching; hence David: To the sinner God said: Why do you declare my justices? etc., Psalm 49. Scab or ringworm. The fornicator is signified, who defiles his body. For he that fornicates sins against his own body, 1 Corinthians 6. You shall not offer them to the Lord. Septuagint: They shall not offer these to the Lord: for such are not to be offered to the ministry of the altar. The sacrifice of peace offerings he does not add as above, that we may understand this said of the ministers of the altar, who ought to be holocaust, and lead a perfect and consummated life. With ear and tail cut off, etc. Cut off in the ear is he who is disobedient, who delights in foul words, turns away from good. Voluntarily, etc. Such a one either does the commandments, and is called ox; or is simple, and is called sheep. Therefore we do not altogether oppose, or reckon on the enemy's side, but teach and exhort. Or bruised, etc. He who yields to temptations brought upon him and loses strength of soul. For it is not fitting to suffer these, nor yield to the afflicting enemy. Hence: Why do I go sorrowful while the enemy afflicts me? Psalm 41. And cut. He who by one wicked action as with a knife cuts himself off from union with God, deprived of the offspring of virtue and the signs of manhood: for different is he who is gradually worn down.
22.27: 22.27 Ox, sheep, and goat. ISICHIUS. The mother of all is nature, etc., down to hence Solomon: Praise not a man before his death, Ecclesiasticus 11.
22.28: 22.28 They shall not be sacrificed. ISICHIUS. It signifies the legal Passover, because Moses delivered these to the Jews to be immolated on the day of the Passover, saying: You shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God; sheep, etc., Deuteronomy 16.: this Passover those cannot celebrate who have received the true. In one day, etc. THE SAME. Because the old Passover had its time, etc., down to: On the morrow they crucified Christ.
23.1: 23.1 These are the feasts of the Lord. ISICHIUS. If you attend subtly to the present, etc., down to rests on the intelligible sabbath.
23.4: 23.4 These are therefore. Not of the Lord, as all the others, but of the Lord properly, in which, the enemy being conquered, he saved the human race and brought it back from captivity, Exodus 2.
23.5: 23.5 On the fourteenth day, etc. ISICHIUS. Let us ask the Jews, etc., down to in which Christ our Passover was sacrificed, etc. It is the Phase of the Lord. Because the Lord suffered, he did not at once finish the times, but left the remnants of the last hour and of the evening, that their sound may go out into all the earth, Psalm 18., of the apostles, namely, and their words unto the ends of the world. Toward evening also, or in the middle of the evening, anticipating his own Passover he celebrated his cross, because he delivered to the disciples the mystic, the true Passover. It was night, therefore, when Judas, having taken the morsel, went out to betray: the next day he fulfilled the Passover. Hence on the fifteenth day the lawgiver established this feast, and proclaimed the solemnity of unleavened bread.
23.6: 23.6 Seven days, etc. If we truly wish to celebrate the Passover, for seven days, that is always, we ought to be unleavened from all malice, and chiefly from the Jewish error. Hence the Apostle says: Not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, 1 Corinthians 5.
23.7: 23.7 Any work, etc. He that commits sin is the servant of sin, John 8. We ought not to serve sin when we celebrate the Passover, in which Christ freed us from sin. Servile, etc. He does not permit servile things to be done on other days on which he forbade us, hence he adds: but you shall offer sacrifice by fire to the Lord.
23.8: 23.8 Sacrifice, etc. Septuagint: holocausts, where it is hinted that he commands to cease from all servile things; moreover he named not only the first but the seventh, to include the whole of human life, because this is the beginning, this the end, in which all can be comprehended.
23.11: 23.11 On the morrow. He could have said the second of unleavened bread: but lest he lead our intent to the following day, to the morrow, namely, of the first, he said on the other day, signifying the resurrection which succeeded the passion, as day to day.
23.12: 23.12 And on the same day. Of the resurrection, that is of the lifting up of the sheaf, that is, when we celebrate the resurrection we must not forget the Lord's sacrifice, from which the sheaf was offered.
23.13: 23.13 Two tenths. For perfect humanity and perfect divinity must come together into one: in oil, that is, through the mercy he had for us; so the sacrifice is found a sweet odor to the Lord, if we understand what is worthy of him. Libations also. Behold the intelligible offering of Melchizedek, which is accomplished in bread and wine, Genesis 14.; hence a fourth part is offered, that by the fourth part the evangelical doctrine may be signified; by the libation the Lord's word, in which he says: This is my blood, which shall be shed for many unto remission of sins, Matthew 26.
23.14: 23.14 Bread. The offering of the present gifts, which is the mystery of Christ, has reconciled us to God, and prepared new food. Parched corn. Septuagint: you shall not eat new parched grain, or ground and cleaned by hands: for so chidra, others interpret, because the commands of Christ seek action and correction, Matthew 11.
23.16: 23.16 Fifty days, and so, etc. This is the Lord's day, on which we celebrate the feast of Pentecost, which the Jews celebrate neither according to the letter nor the spirit, who do not number the days according to the law. You shall offer a new sacrifice, new, not old, not secular. For the Spirit coming renewed the whole human life, because he confirmed the institution of Christ, and in them perfected the confirmation of life: hence, He shall receive of mine, and shall declare it to you, John 16. Therefore he came not on another day, but on which the resurrection was, and the intelligible sheaf offered, to show that the new conversation was perfected by the resurrection of Christ and the coming of the Holy Spirit.
23.17: 23.17 From your habitations, etc. Because there is a chief habitation, of which it is said: Blessed are they that dwell in your house, O Lord, Psalm 82. And elsewhere: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek, that I may dwell, etc., Psalm 26. Loaves of first-fruits. For the Lord first perfected and taught the Gospel with the law. You have heard that it was said to them of old: You shall not kill: But I say to you: Whosoever is angry with his brother shall be in danger of the judgment, Matthew 5.: for hence he joined the law to the Gospel. Hence Luke says: What Jesus began to do and to teach, etc., Acts 1. Of two tenths, etc. Of doctrine, namely, which teaches perfect divinity and perfect humanity, nor can they otherwise be baked than by such doctrine.
23.18: 23.18 Seven lambs. For the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, which he calls lambs, because the Holy Spirit is one with Christ, of whom it is written: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sin of the world, therefore no one can say Lord Jesus but in the Holy Spirit, John 1; 1 Corinthians 12. And two rams. By whom the enemy is winnowed. These are the higher commandments, and virtues, which others follow as sheep, for example: Go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, Matthew 9. With libations, etc. Which are knowledge and correction; hence: But thanks be to God, who manifests the odor of his knowledge by us, for we are the good odor of Christ, etc., 2 Corinthians 2.
23.19: 23.19 And two lambs, etc. The commandments of peace and holiness, hence: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, etc., Hebrews 12. These, because said in apostolic speech, he commands to be offered with the loaves of the first-fruits, which signify the doctrine of Christ. Hence in what follows: And when the priest shall have lifted them up with the loaves of the first-fruits, John 10.
23.20: 23.20 They shall go to the use, etc. To the use of that priest, that is, of Christ, who is our priest and our Lord: his are the loaves of first-fruits and the lambs of the commandments, he spoke in Paul, he offered all that was said; first he announced peace to the disciples, and kept holiness, as the Holy of holies.
23.21: 23.21 Most solemn. In which the calling of the Gentiles was not only foretold but fulfilled: when Parthians and Medes and Elamites and the other nations heard the apostles speaking the wonderful works of God in various tongues, Acts 2.
23.22: 23.22 After, etc. He seems to have said the same above, but there: You shall not complete your reaping; here, however, he says: You shall not cut it to the ground, and the very change of words hints the difference. The harvest of the land, etc. Of conversation, whose reaping after the resurrection of Christ and the coming of the Holy Spirit, yet the word of preaching does not deliver all the knowledge which we are to have in the future. For there are things that cannot now be revealed to us, Matthew 8., hence in the aforesaid festivities he interposed this law. For the poor and the strangers. Septuagint: for the poor and the proselyte, that is Christ, who had not where to lay his head, and came unto his own, and his own received him not. Here he understands only those who remain; hence: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways! Romans 11.
23.24: 23.24 In the seventh month, the first day of the month. Seven signifies consummation, whether special or general. Hence God rested on the seventh day, Genesis 2.; and by his rest signified ours; hence: He that has entered into his rest, has rested from his works, as God did from his, Hebrews 4. The beginning of the consummation of times is the Lord's coming, hence: Little children, it is the last hour, 1 John 2. This time he calls the first of the seventh month, as the beginning of consummation is also rest to us, whom it made to cease from evil works, and freed from a heavy yoke; hence: Come to me, all you that labor and are burdened, etc., and learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart, and you shall find rest to your souls, Matthew 11. With sounding trumpets. Because it preaches the resurrection of the Savior, which is the memorial of the general resurrection, which according to the Apostle will be at the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God, etc.
23.25: 23.25 You shall do no servile work therein. As if [as] there is no work of doing servile things: you did before, but as you yielded your members to iniquity unto iniquity, so now yield to serve justice unto sanctification, Romans 6.: for this is the true holocaust.
23.27: 23.27 On the tenth day, etc. ISICHIUS. That propitiation and deliverance from sins is acquired in humility and affliction of soul we understand from this. This we ought to do from the evening, that is begin with penance, which Christ made the beginning of his preaching, Matthew 4.: upon penance a good life consummated in virtues is to be built. Hence he added: And you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.
23.28: 23.28 The day of propitiation. ISICHIUS. It signifies two things, that in this time we shall receive propitiation, and therefore in that we ought to abstain from all evil.
23.31: 23.31 Nothing therefore. It signifies that we must always cease from evil and superfluous things. Hence the Lord also neither grants to plead a cause, nor to think what to eat or drink or wear, for he announced the true sabbath of sabbaths.
23.32: 23.32 You shall afflict. It is a recapitulation of humility, which is the foundation and base of virtues. Hence the Lord says: Whosoever shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven, Matthew 18.
23.34: 23.34 From the fifteenth day. ISICHIUS. By this number the feast is begun, etc., down to a building not made with hands is had in heaven, 2 Corinthians 5.
23.36: 23.36 The day also. THE SAME. Note that the same is said of the first and of the eighth, because, namely, the day of the resurrection is second, and the beginning of the age to come. The first, in Christ, is the beginning of conversation and the opening of the things to come; the eighth succeeds the present age, which is signified in the seven. Besides, the saints have rest and the future life in this life. Hence to the apostles it was said: The kingdom of God is within you, etc. Assembly. Septuagint: going out, because hence is the departure, there the dwelling, hence: I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, Philippians 1.
23.37: 23.37 These are the feasts of the Lord, etc. THE SAME. Paul agrees with the lawgiver, etc., down to either in perils, or we promise voluntarily.
23.39: 23.39 From the fifteenth, etc. The fifteenth, composed of seven and eight, signifies the evangelical preaching, which consists of the present life and the future, composes this, prepares that. On the first day and on the eighth day. THE SAME. Which is the eighth, etc., down to because rest in the future is kept for the faithful doing the law.
23.40: 23.40 On the first day the fruit. THE SAME. The fruit is Christ, etc., down to in its season. And branches of palm trees, etc. The sprouts of justice growing young, because the just shall flourish like the palm; but because nothing is rejected from the palm, nor from those who live justly, he adds, and boughs of thick trees. And boughs of a tree. All the fruits of virtues, namely, but chiefly mercy, which ought to be continuous and permanent. Hence: Let not oil fail from your head, Ecclesiastes 9. Of the torrent, etc. Of the present life, namely, which flows like a torrent, boiling with temptations and tribulations, hence: He shall drink of the torrent in the way, therefore shall he lift up his head, Psalm 109., on the cross, namely, hanging.
24.2: 24.2 Command the children of Israel. ISICHIUS. The candlestick is the evangelical life, etc., down to where the merciful hide treasures.
24.3: 24.3 Until morning, of the age to come: for then there will not be a time of praying or of giving alms, hence: Say not to your friend, Go, and come again, and tomorrow I will give to you: for you know not what the day to come may bring forth, Proverbs 3, 27.
24.4: 24.4 Upon the candlestick, etc. Christ, who is the true light and enlightens every man that comes into the world. And he did no sin, neither was guile found, etc., Isaiah 53. Over this burns the lamp, that is the Holy Spirit, who appeared in fiery tongues over the disciples: to this we must offer the purest oil, that is a clean life, knowing that not all can kindle that fire, but Christ alone and his sons, who, full of the Spirit, says, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, Isaiah 61. Who also says, I am come to cast fire on the earth, and what will I but that it be kindled? Luke 12. Breathing on them, as kindling, he says: Receive the Holy Spirit, etc., John 20. This lamp is not kindled except by a clean life and conversation, or if kindled is soon put out, hence: Extinguish not the Spirit, etc., 1 Thessalonians 5.
24.5: 24.5 You shall take also. BEDE, book I on the Tabernacle, ch. 7, vol. 2. The twelve loaves on the table of the tabernacle, etc., down to that through labors and good works of temporal life we may hasten to it. You shall bake of it twelve. ORIGEN, hom. 13 on Exodus. The word of the Lord is bread, but manifold, etc., down to the bread is set on a clean table, namely, upon a holy and pure mind.
24.10: 24.10 And behold, etc. ISICHIUS. The Israelite woman, etc., down to who is blasphemed in Christ. And behold. ORIGEN, hom. 14 on Leviticus. Two quarrel: one wholly an Israelite, etc., down to for sometimes he who is cast out is within; and he who is without seems to be held within.
24.12: 24.12 And they put him, etc. Moses does not pronounce sentence against the blasphemer by his own authority, but reserving it to the command of God, puts him in prison: for the law hates him who blasphemes, against whom it frequently preaches the Trinity, but not manifestly like the Gospel; therefore it reserved him to the judgment of the Gospel. He that believes not in the Son is already judged, John 3, and the like.
24.15: 24.15 The man who, etc. The expression is as if it were said: that man or that man, that is whoever man. Not as some think, man man is so said as in praise, as if man; but man man, that is of whatever sort, as one even like to cattle, but who truly is a man, which sense is not true, but this is plainly shown here to be a form of speech of the Scriptures, since it is said of him who is blamed, not who is praised. Man, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 87 on Leviticus. If he curse his God, he shall bear his sin. And he that names the name of the Lord, let him die the death; as if it were one thing to curse his God, etc., down to the kind of speech is to be noted. ISICHIUS. Septuagint: Man man, etc., down to as the son of the Israelite woman named and blasphemed, Joshua 7.
24.17: 24.17 He that strikes and kills a man. Septuagint: He that smites the soul of a man, etc., that is, who has drawn to iniquity. By soul he understands the animal man, who perceives not the things that are of the Spirit of God. AUGUSTINE, question 88 on Leviticus. He that smites the soul of a man and he be dead, etc. He does not say, etc., down to for this is the soul of man to be struck.
24.20: 24.20 Breach, etc. Septuagint: Contrition for contrition, that is, if by teaching, persuading, scandalizing he has crushed any virtue of his neighbor. Tooth for tooth. The power of speaking. For teeth are taken for words, hence: The sons of men, their teeth are weapons and arrows, etc., Psalm 59. And his eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk, Genesis 49. For clearer and plainer are the words of the Gospel than the milk of the law.
24.21: 24.21 He that strikes, etc. According to the letter these were necessary for the Jews, who could not take: If one strike you on the right cheek, turn to him also the other, Matthew 5. But being malevolent, they wished to inflict evil and not to suffer. Therefore by fear of reciprocal punishment they had to be called back from crime.
24.23: 24.23 And they brought out, etc. By the very experience he shows the law confirmed, that you too may fear to blaspheme and flee sin, which not only the prince but the whole multitude avenges. For all in common ought to punish blasphemers, who did not fear to detract from the author of all, and to separate all from him.
25.1: 25.1 And the Lord spoke, etc. When you are entered, etc. ISICHIUS. The land, good conversation, of which it is said: Your good Spirit shall lead me into the land, etc., Psalm 142.
25.3: 25.3 Six years, etc. While we are in this life, we are in the visible creation, which the number six signifies. For in six days all things that are seen were created: but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of the land to the Lord. For when after the present time the sabbath shall come, of which Paul says: There remains a sabbath-rest for the people of God, which the seventh day signifies, on which God rested from all his works, the visible, namely, Hebrews 4., there will be no more a time of working. You shall sow your field, etc. By field and vineyard, since he forbade the one to be sown and the other pruned, every kind of field is to be understood: for neither in an olive grove nor in any field of another kind is anything to be worked.
25.5: 25.5 What grows of itself, etc. Of those things, namely, which we do here, in the future we shall eat the fruit; hence: For you shall eat the labors of your hands, blessed are you, and it shall be well with you, Psalm 127.
25.6: 25.6 But they shall be, etc. He does not forbid the Lord's people to eat what is of itself, but to lay it up for private use.
25.8: 25.8 You shall number also. Let us ask the Jews, if the lawgiver honored the seventh day as they say and commanded rest from works, why he commanded the fiftieth year to be celebrated: for seven weeks make forty-nine years. It would not be fitting therefore to rest in the fiftieth unless the law signified a mystery which the weakness of the Jews could not grasp. For a twofold consummation of all visible things by God is signified; one singular of each, another common to all, when there will be no time of working; in the above he hints the first, in these the second. Seven. In a week of days the human age is divided. When therefore this number multiplied in itself, and the whole age of the world completed, and time rolled on has come to its end, the fiftieth succeeds as the forty-ninth year, in which will be the resurrection, hence he adds: And sounding the trumpet in the seventh month, etc. Hence the Apostle: At the trumpet of God they shall descend from heaven, and the dead who are in Christ shall rise incorruptible, 1 Thessalonians 4. For the trumpet must go before the one raising: therefore in the forty-ninth year, in which is the common consummation, he commanded the trumpet to sound.
25.9: 25.9 In the seventh month. Because in the seventh month, as it were, of the age of the world Christ came; the first month, which was in paradise; the second until the flood; the third until Abraham; the fourth until the descent into Egypt; the fifth until the transmigration, the sixth until the coming of Christ; the seventh the coming itself.
25.10: 25.10 And you shall sanctify the year. As if in holiness it is to be awaited and thought of, for we ought to follow peace and holiness, Hebrews 12., without which no man shall see God. Every one. Of the patriarchs and prophets there is a certain hospitable family, over which Abraham presides. There is another of chastity, over which Joseph presides. There is another of meekness, over which Moses presides, Genesis 18, 39; Numbers 12.
25.14: 25.14 When you sell, etc. Anyone can sell or buy. Hence Paul: All things are yours, as you are ours, 1 Corinthians 3. This according to the letter he forms morally, that in contracts we sympathize with our neighbors, that no one too troublesome traffic upon the needs of the poor, nor strive to acquire the possessions of others, but lend to the needy, and receive back the loans gradually from the fruits of the fields. According to the number ISICHIUS. That is according to the strength of each. For the years signify the age, in which is shown what each can do according to the body.
25.16: 25.16 The more THE SAME. That is, if he can work much, he will exact much fruit; if he cannot much, he will repay little; for this one shall bear thirtyfold, that sixtyfold, that a hundredfold, Matthew 13.
25.18: 25.18 Do my precepts. Lest anyone, hearing of the moderation in selling and buying, grow the slacker, and the condescension itself do harm, he cautiously adds: Do my precepts, etc. For he wishes no one idle, but to bear fruit according to strength. Each one's conscience also examines strength. And my judgments, etc. THE SAME. Not corrupting their intention or operation; as if someone gives alms, let him not harm one to profit another: for the precept which commanded alms to be given willed it to be just. But if you say, etc. THE SAME. Because he had commanded the land to rest two years, lest they be disturbed as anxious what they should eat or what they should drink, he says: I will give my blessing, etc., Matthew 6. And it is to be noted that while Christ says: Be not solicitous for tomorrow, the law commands them not to be solicitous for three years.
25.21: 25.21 I will give my blessing. THE SAME. Christ. Hence we have blessed you in the name of the Lord, that is Christ, who is the name of the Father. Who named the Father to us and manifested him; this one came in the sixth year, that is in perfection, which the number six signifies; and to reform man whom he had formed on the sixth day, that there it is called the sixth day, here the sixth year, because between our formation and reformation many times flowed by.
25.23: 25.23 The land also. AUGUSTINE, question 90 on Leviticus. Other codices have, etc., down to whoever has, ought to use.
25.25: 25.25 If impoverished. ISICHIUS. What our substance is, etc., down to teaches how he may restore. He can redeem. ISICHIUS. According to that, etc., down to that it may in a way be common.
25.28: 25.28 Until the year. A year, because it has in itself all hours, and days and months, and all revolutions, signifies perfection. A sin either perfect and long-lasting is corrected by nothing but perfect penance, in which fasting, prayer, sackcloth, alms and tears are performed: for through these full remission is acquired.
25.29: 25.29 He that shall sell a house. THE SAME. The seller is not expressed, nor is neighbor or kinsman said. For it is not one, but the whole people: nor of the kinship of the Jews, but of Sodom and Gomorrah. He that shall sell a house, etc. In the preceding chapter he expounded the spiritual conversation of each, here he intends to treat generally of the synagogue or Church, because the Church of the Gentiles receives freedom, the synagogue serves forever, except the Levites, that is the apostles, and those who cling to them. ORIGEN, hom. 15 on Leviticus. He that shall sell a house, etc. Of Jacob it is written, etc., down to they always receive penance and are always redeemed.
25.31: 25.31 By the law of the fields. ISICHIUS. Because in the Gospel they are neighbors, not in the law. Therefore they can always be redeemed, and from when Christ came until the second coming they are redeemed by parts. Septuagint: They shall be reckoned to the field of the land, of which, namely, it is said: The kingdom of heaven is like to a treasure hidden in a field, that is the Gospel, in which the treasure is the mystery of Christ.
25.32: 25.32 The houses of the Levites. ORIGEN, hom. 15 on Leviticus. If it be a priestly house or Levitical, etc., down to the satisfaction, namely, of desire.
25.34: 25.34 The suburbs. ISICHIUS. Other fields, that is conversations of virtues and of doctrine. These are separate from their cities, which subsist through them and are saved, and are not sold, because freely received, freely given.
25.35: 25.35 If impoverished. THE SAME. Marvel at the wisdom and piety of the lawgiver; in lowly things he expounds sublime ones, but according to the letter he gives a rule of piety. Who brought out. As if he said: As I freed you from the dominion of the Egyptians, and, sinners being cast out, brought you into the land of the Canaanites already commanded, so I will not have you held under the dominion of sinners, nor embrace the society of sinners, but when they wish to repent, sustain them by cohabitation and bestowal of means.
25.39: 25.39 If by poverty. The letter is full of great piety, but the spiritual understanding is fuller.
25.40: 25.40 But as a hireling. Each is subject, but yet this one is free: so he who was converted through you is indeed subject, but by the dignity of divine grace is a brother.
25.43: 25.43 Afflict not, etc., because in what you judge, you shall be judged: and with the same measure that you mete, it shall be measured to you again, Matthew 7.
25.44: 25.44 Man-servant and maid-servant. ISICHIUS. He shows what difference there is between those whom we save for God from the unbelievers, and those already faithful and like to us in the dignity of calling and conversation, whom for a time, weakened in virtues, we correct: for these work with us until the jubilee, those are servants forever.
25.45: 25.45 Of them that. ISICHIUS. The kinsmen of the Jews are the heretics, who preach with us the same mysteries, as though in our land: but believe not rightly and perfectly. These you shall have. THE SAME. Those whom we convert from the Gentiles or Jews or heretics we acquire forever as servants and handmaids: because for them we spend the money of doctrine, and can hand them over to our sons, that is disciples, to be taught, as Paul committed the Cretans to Titus, the Ephesians to Timothy to be taught.
25.46: 25.46 But your brethren. As if they will not be of the same dignity with you, whom you converted from the impious, and whom you repaired when they fell.
25.47: 25.47 If grown strong. THE SAME. That is, if newly joined to your faith, a Gentile, or Jew, or heretic, shall have become famous for virtues, that he can reprove and exhort. If grown strong, etc. According to the letter it shows how much he loves liberty. For therefore he does not permit an Israelite to serve strangers, but commands him to be redeemed. Who will. It is shameful for a man nourished in the faith from infancy to submit to the mastery of such as have suddenly become masters, hence Jerome: Yesterday in the forum, today at the altar; yesterday companion of actors, today consecrator of virgins.
25.49: 25.49 Uncle, etc. THE SAME. The paternal cousins are those who begot us in the faith, their brothers the like preachers, the sons of the brothers the disciples of like. Kinsman. THE SAME. Who is more remote than uncle or cousin, but nearer than an in-law. For he who has not care of his own, and especially of his household, has denied the faith, 1 Timothy 5. In-law. THE SAME. In kinship of faith of the incarnation of Christ, who are of his flesh and bones. But if. THE SAME. For our freedom and glory the Holy Spirit acts, and commands any servant of sin to be redeemed by virtues. And himself. THE SAME. He who has become poor in sin, when before he was rich in virtue and doctrine, rightly frees himself while by exhorting and counseling he recalls to virtue.
25.50: 25.50 Reckoning. THE SAME. That is, considering with himself by what virtue, etc., down to therefore the Lord says to him: This day is salvation come to this house.
25.51: 25.51 He shall pay. THE SAME. According to what he sinned, he must pay the price. What gluttony sinned let fasting correct; what talkativeness admitted let silence blot out, and in like manner contraries are cured by contraries.
26.1: 26.1 You shall not make. He forbids the worship of idols both visible and invisible. Graven thing. ISICHIUS. In the buildings of houses and the possessions of fields wishing to carve some memorial of yourselves. Nor a notable. THE SAME. A heap of gold and silver or precious stones in which the covetous are seduced, as the Gentiles in idols.
26.2: 26.2 Keep. ISICHIUS. By abstaining from all evil and resting in all good: for this is the true sabbath.
26.3: 26.3 If in my precepts. He foretold what ought to be done, what avoided. At the end he enumerates what rewards are due to the observers, what punishments to the transgressors. If in my precepts. THE SAME. These cannot stand according to the letter, etc., down to which are signified in this chapter. ORIGEN, hom. 16 on Leviticus. If the law is carnal, etc., down to John came in the spirit and power of Elijah. My commandments. Such as that: He that keeps not the sabbath, let him be stoned by all the synagogue, and the like. I will give you rains, etc. And I will give is superfluous, by the custom of our speech, but added after the manner of Scriptures. In their seasons. ORIGEN. In due time, not when drunken, not occupied in other things: prudently therefore let the teacher judge to whom he is to minister rain, and measure of wheat, and to whom he ought to give milk, let him not give meat.
26.4: 26.4 The earth shall bring forth. Septuagint: The trees of the field shall give their fruit. THE SAME. The motions of the soul, which are higher than the motions of the earth, that is of our flesh, whose fruits are charity, justice, meekness and the like. Fruit trees. ORIGEN. A tree cannot, etc., down to of which it is said: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her.
26.5: 26.5 The threshing of your harvest shall reach. ORIGEN. The soul that sprouts from the word of God, etc., down to remain to be dispensed in time with fellow-servants. It shall reach. For bread strengthens the heart of man, wine makes glad, Psalm 103. What is said of continence, of observances and keeping of the commandments seems grain, of which bread is made that strengthens hearts. But those which pertain to knowledge and gladden the mind by exploration of hidden things are compared to wine and vintage. For the heart rejoices when obscure [hidden] things are explained. Vintage. The fruit of the soul. For the vintage is a tree. To have these together, that is to bear fruit in body and soul, is a great blessing. ISICHIUS. For the soul gathering its virtues soon desires others. Hence: Forgetting the things that are behind, I stretch forth myself to those that are before, Philippians 3. Vintage. ORIGEN. As if we say, etc., down to that of the spirit we may reap life everlasting. Your bread. That which came down from heaven and gives life to the world; not that which abounds more in evils than goods. Without fear. If the body is stable and the soul bears fruit, we shall be secure in our land, because the flesh will not lust against the spirit, Galatians 4.
26.6: 26.6 And the sword shall not. ISICHIUS. Because there shall be peace in your borders; now from concupiscences are wars and quarrels.
26.7: 26.7 Your enemies. THE SAME. Slain by fasting, prayer, and the like; hence: This kind is not cast out but by prayer and fasting, Matthew 17. They shall fall. Septuagint: In your sight by your death, namely by the mortifying of your members which are upon the earth, that is fornication, uncleanness, and the like, Colossians 3.
26.8: 26.8 They shall pursue. ORIGEN. As the number five indicates the wise and the foolish, etc., down to lest believers be deceived. ISICHIUS. Septuagint, etc., down to can pursue and conquer. And a hundred. Who have not only subtle knowledge but also a perfect life, who are spiritually without blame, and therefore are called a hundred, namely those who bring forth hundredfold fruits.
26.9: 26.9 I will look. Whose look is salvation. The Lord looked on Peter, and he wept bitterly. If the sun does not look on the crop, it remains fruitless. God looks on the crop of our heart, and with the rays of his word enlightens us, increases and multiplies that we may become great; as Isaac became great, and Moses great, and John great. Increase. In good works, that small things may become great. Hence: What you did to one of these my least, etc., Matthew 25. You shall be multiplied. That few things may become great or many. Hence: If there be any other commandment, it is comprised in this word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself, Romans 13.
26.10: 26.10 You shall eat. ORIGEN. The old law and the prophets, etc., down to and put on the new.
26.11: 26.11 I will set. If we have the aforesaid, the old man being cast off, our heart is renewed: God comes to us and dwells in us, Colossians 3. He shall not cast away, etc. ORIGEN. I dare to say that the soul of God is Christ, as also the Word of God the wisdom of God and the power of God, 1 Corinthians 1. It is therefore as if he said: My Son shall not cast you away. Soul. AUGUSTINE, question 93 on Leviticus. God calls his soul, etc., down to who say Jesus had not a soul.
26.12: 26.12 I will walk. ISICHIUS. Made man. Hence: This is our God, and there shall no other be accounted of in comparison of him; afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men, Baruch 3.
26.14: 26.14 But if. ISICHIUS. The goods of the obedient he expressed in the preceding chapter: what the evils of transgressors are he shows in the present, some of which the Jews suffered literally: all, however, according to the spirit.
26.16: 26.16 In want. THE SAME. Of the word of God. Hence: This saying is hard, and who can hear it? John 6. Because they transgressed the understanding of the law, to make the evangelical testament void, he spoke obscurely to them, that they might not understand.
26.17: 26.17 You shall flee, none. THE SAME. Because the Gentiles do not pursue to expel, but hasten their salvation, according to that: But I follow after, if I may by any means apprehend, Philippians 3. But if. THE SAME. He frequently uses distinctions of this kind, etc., down to signifies full and entire vengeance.
26.18: 26.18 I will add correction. Septuagint: And I will add to chastise you seven times, etc. Here too it is superfluous. Seven times, however, is to be taken for every number.
26.19: 26.19 And I will break the pride of your stubbornness. Because you say: We are the seed of Abraham, and we have never been slaves to any man, John 3.: therefore you shall serve the Gentiles.
26.23: 26.23 A sword, of the spirit, which is the word of God, which through the preachers convinces the Jews, that they may not contradict holding the Old Testament with the Gospel. I will send into cities. The prophets, in whom the faithful find fortifications and salvation, the enemies fleeing are taken, there they die, unable to resist the prophets clearly speaking of Christ.
26.26: 26.26 So that ten, etc. ISICHIUS. They have not the bread of doctrine, etc., down to therefore those nourished with these breads are not satisfied.
26.27: 26.27 But if, etc. THE SAME. Moses is not only lawgiver, etc., down to and blasphemed the author of the law.
26.29: 26.29 The flesh of your sons. That is disciples, whom you take to yourselves as sons, you shall bring to the same doctrine by strong words which corrupt the soul.
26.30: 26.30 You shall fall among ruins. For the people fall with the Pharisees falling spiritually, whom the people admired as idols, intent on their traditions.
26.31: 26.31 Your cities. According to the letter, or the books of the prophets, in which they find not the fruit of holiness.
26.34: 26.34 Then shall the land keep its sabbaths, that is rest, you keeping holiday, namely, and removed from the law, when in the law and prophets you find not your will.
26.36: 26.36 It shall terrify them. As a leaf hides the fruit, so the letter hides the spirit: take away the leaf, take the fruit. The sound of a flying leaf. Hyperbole: because they will dread even the lightest things. They shall fall none pursuing. For we do not pursue them, but follow that we may recall them.
26.37: 26.37 They shall fall. When we dispute with them they bring diverse testimonies by turns: but they will be confused by alternate words, one confounding the other while he seems to help.
26.41: 26.41 Their uncircumcised mind. Because uncircumcised in heart, defiled by the foreskin of vices, for it is not the circumcision which is in the flesh, Romans 2. Then shall they pray for their impieties. Septuagint: They shall take their sins as pleasing, the punishments, namely, which they shall suffer for their sins.
26.42: 26.42 That I made with Jacob. ISICHIUS. Note that he changed the order of time and race, etc., down to but they are joined as akin and fitting. I will remember the land also. ISICHIUS. Of Scripture, namely, which I will commit to the cast-out Jews, who transgressed it or were transgressing it and wrongly interpreted it.
26.44: 26.44 Yet even when they were in the enemy's land. Well at the end of the chapter he soothes, and those whom he had terrified with threats he consoles with promises. Not utterly. Blindness in part has happened in Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles should come in; and the rest, 1 Timothy 2. Nor so have I despised. I who will the salvation of all: therefore after so great iniquities I save even the remnants of the Jews.
26.45: 26.45 These are. ISICHIUS. Until a certain time, etc., down to not by dissolving but by fulfilling. In Mount Sinai. Not in Sion. Hence: The God of gods shall be seen in Sion, Psalm 83. And elsewhere: Out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty. God shall come manifestly, Psalm 49. And in Malachi: The Lord whom you seek shall suddenly come to his temple, Malachi 3.
27.2: 27.2 The man who. ISICHIUS. These words are full of prudence: what ought to be done or not he commanded above; now he expounds the dignity of those who act, wholly or in part, what difference the perfect life, the middling, the beginning has in knowledge of God he describes also the differences of ages. Soul. ISICHIUS. Aquila and Theodotion, admirable. Symmachus, if he separate himself. Septuagint: the honor of his soul. From the twentieth. THE SAME. When the youth is strong, etc., down to of which it is said: Be perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect, Matthew 5. Shekels. ISICHIUS. Or didrachmas, the sixtyfold fruit, etc., down to hence: Let a widow be chosen of not less than sixty years, 1 Timothy 5.
27.5: 27.5 From the fifth. THE SAME. Who is sensible and has begun to advance, but cannot be adorned by the conversation of fasting. Until. THE SAME. Who has begun to advance in the five senses: for he is advanced here to virtue and perfection. For those of twenty years are strong and vigorous. The male shall give twenty shekels. THE SAME. Or didrachmas, that is forty drachmas; that is four hundred obols. Forty, however, signifies the gain of fasting and prayers. For so many days Moses fasted, Exodus 34., and Elijah, 3 Kings 19., and Christ himself, and afterwards was tempted by the devil, Matthew 4.
27.7: 27.7 The woman ten. THE SAME. Or didrachmas, that is twenty drachmas or two hundred obols, the keeping, namely, of the ten commandments, which are doubled according to the letter and the spirit, in which fasting is not commanded, because it befits the advanced not yet the perfect. From one. It is of one month, who is now begotten in the faith, to whom it is said: As newborn babes, desire the rational milk without guile, etc., 1 Peter 2. Five. Or didrachmas, namely that the male have a double sense, and what he hears sensibly he receive intelligibly. So he is led to perfection, wherefore his price is a hundred obols: a hundred, however, is perfect. For the woman. THE SAME. For the woman three didrachmas, etc., down to as now sharers of the evangelical conversation. Sixty. Who promised excellence of conversation, like virginity or renunciation of the world, but is weakened. He shall give fifteen. Or didrachmas, which are thirty drachmas. For the good land rendered three fruits, Matthew 13.: a hundredfold, that is to be a virgin or renounce the world; sixtyfold, continence; thirtyfold, the conversation of chaste wedlock.
27.8: 27.8 If poor. Who has sinned much, therefore Aquila interpreted, if he has exceeded. He shall stand. For if we offer anyone subject to us to the service of God, we ought not to receive him back into our service, promising for him either better or less good. As much as he shall estimate. That is, as much as he sees he can, he will impose of satisfaction: but if he is rich, that he distribute money, if healthy that he fast, pray, labor.
27.9: 27.9 Animal. Because he has expounded the differences of offerings which are from ourselves and the degrees: now he expounds when the offering of those who are subject to us as cattle is holy. It shall be holy. According to the law unblemished and clean: as if we offer to God a son, disciple, servant, or anyone subject to us.
27.10: 27.10 Which. That the offering be double, and the enemy blush, who suggested changing the offering.
27.11: 27.11 An unclean animal. ISICHIUS. Which not together, etc., down to that it may be offered to the Lord. It is to be known that to be sanctified is one thing, to be holy another, to be offered to God another, to be God's another. For what is sanctified and offered begins to be holy, which it was not, and is gradually increased. What is holy and God's needs no increase, because it is perfect. It is good therefore to be sanctified by the teaching and help of others, but better to be such that one can sanctify oneself and others, which is of few. He sanctifies a house to the Lord who wills his household and kin, both sensible and intelligible, to live purely and holily, that it may be the Church of God. If, however, he is not fit of himself to do this, the priest must consider whether it be good or bad. For it consists of diverse persons, and according as they can he ought to enjoin on them.
27.13: 27.13 A fifth part. The mind, namely, which rules the five senses, without which the foolish virgins are not received to the wedding, Matthew 25.
27.14: 27.14 If a man vow. ISICHIUS. In what follows he says: Everything consecrated to the Lord, whether man or animal or field, cannot be redeemed; here however he commands a house and field to be redeemed. But perhaps he decrees this according to the diverse intentions of the offerers, as there he has no will of having further what he utterly consecrated.
27.15: 27.15 But if he, etc. ISICHIUS. To redeem is to free the household by doctrine and rule of life, and wash away whatever opposes holiness. He shall add, however, to the admonition and edification of the priest understanding and frequent remembrance.
27.16: 27.16 But if a field. That is divine Scripture, whose vine is Christ, the Father the husbandman, John 14. In this is hidden the treasure, that is the saving preaching: in this each one's possession is diverse, the mode namely of knowing which each has been able to obtain for himself. If with thirty measures, etc. THE SAME. In thirty measures of barley the Old Testament. In fifty shekels or didrachmas according to the Septuagint understand spiritual and perfect doctrine. But when this rule is to be given perfectly or diminished, understand from what follows: If immediately from the year of the beginning jubilee, etc.
27.17: 27.17 If immediately from the year. THE SAME. That is, if the way of grace, etc., down to offering to the priest, it shall be possessed by him.
