27.19: 27.19 He shall add the fifth part. The proper understanding of the priest's doctrine: for by the doctrine and instruction of the priest we are first governed, but afterwards we ought to advance and add our own understanding.
27.20: 27.20 But if, etc. THE SAME. He consecrates the field and redeems the field, etc., down to for the gain is his who continually governs.
27.22: 27.22 And not of his possession. Because it had been neither of the keeping of his elders nor of the buyer himself.
27.23: 27.23 The priest shall reckon. Rightly the priest reckons with him who warned his brother to penance the true redemption, how, namely, he ought to repent. For he who corrected knows strictly his action and conversation: this one, as priest, the perfect redemption. According to the number of years. From what Scripture preaches of penance, namely: for that estimation is of the jubilee or remission. And he who had vowed shall give it to the Lord. He does not say they shall give, but he shall give. For though by the common counsel of the priest and him who warned to penance the definition of the estimation is given, yet he shall offer who stirred to repent: for he will obey him who is himself bound to the penitent, that he may perfect what he began.
27.24: 27.24 But in the jubilee it shall return to its former lord, etc. Because he is not at once, when penance is given or defined, wholly cleansed, but when it is finished; therefore rightly he says: But in the jubilee, etc., for penance finished and remission received, he shall receive the field of his conversation.
27.25: 27.25 Every estimation shall be weighed by the shekel of the sanctuary. That every definition be made by holy weights, that is those coming from sacred Scripture, for the outward weights, like those of the philosophers or heretics, by which they weigh the truths and perfections of men, are neither holy nor just. A shekel of twenty. That is the ten commandments understood according to the letter and according to the spirit. Whoever refuses either the law or the Gospel has not the didrachma, nor are his weights holy.
27.26: 27.26 The firstborn which. ISICHIUS. The firstborn as our cattle are those who obey us, sons, servants and disciples. But the firstborn of these are those who so obey as to give others example and teaching, of whom elsewhere it is said: Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord, Luke 2. For he opens the womb of sons to be begotten, who begins to obey according to God. Hence Paul of Timothy says: Who is my beloved son in the Lord, he shall put you in mind of my ways, etc., 1 Corinthians 4. No man can sanctify and vow. Not that they are unworthy of sanctification, but that they are holy and need not be sanctified, as a son, who so honors father and mother that he becomes an example to others, as offering honor to God who commanded this, Exodus 20. A servant also who even to carnal masters serves in simplicity of heart, not to the eye, renders service to God himself, Ephesians 6.
27.27: 27.27 But if unclean. ISICHIUS. The sinner, who neither meditates the law as he ought, nor tries to distinguish. Whoever therefore is vehemently obedient to father, lord or master: yet neither meditates the law nor distinguishes, is indeed firstborn among the cattle, but is unclean. And he shall add the fifth part of the price. Offering to him doctrine with understanding, and ruling wisely. For it belongs to a senseless father, lord or master not to teach obedience to those subject to him who belong to him, and not to dispose their life to work according to the law. Let him add therefore to subjection and doctrine understanding: for he alone is clean in the present. Therefore he says: He shall add the fifth part of the price. For obedience has a price: therefore he did not say: the priest shall estimate him, as above.
27.28: 27.28 Everything that is consecrated to the Lord, whether man. ISICHIUS. To anathematize is one thing, etc., down to that is, the conversation of our lot. Whatever once is consecrated. THE SAME. Acquired by right of war, none can despoil the enemy, etc., down to they receive neither increase nor progress.
27.30: 27.30 The Lord's. THE SAME. His, namely, who works the commandments of the law, etc., down to because he knows not what reward he ought to expect.
27.31: 27.31 If any man. THE SAME. According to the letter the lawgiver has interposed many obscure and insoluble things, etc., down to and the fruits of trees in their season.
27.32: 27.32 Under the shepherd's rod. THE SAME. The rod of the cross, etc., down to and are known by him alone who discerns the saints.
27.33: 27.33 It shall not be chosen nor, etc. Because there is none who can be rejected, and what is more to be chosen is not of your discretion. If any change, etc. ISICHIUS. Paul and Barnabas once disagreed, etc., down to writing to Timothy he says: Take Mark and bring him with you: for he is profitable to me for the ministry, 2 Timothy 4. It shall be sanctified to the Lord, etc. THE SAME. Since the course of all is divine, and high, and nearest to the heavenly conversation, in vain do they strive to take away one, bring in another, and consecrate to God the better as it were.
27.34: 27.34 These are the precepts which he commanded, etc. THE SAME. Our disciples, when they are perfect, need nothing of our mastery: therefore he says the firstborn of the unclean are to be redeemed, of the clean however not at all, but neither consecrated to the Lord, nor those last said: for they are shown perfect, because they bear the divine and heavenly intention.
